info.text: Unit 14 — Assessing an Airworthiness Directive. Listening, Reading, Use of English and Vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What does the airworthiness directive order the team to do?

generalfeedback.text: Karlis says the AD "orders a recurring inspection of the landing gear pin". A recurring inspection is a check that must be repeated at set intervals.

answer.text: A recurring inspection of the landing gear pin

feedback.text: Correct. It repeats at a fixed interval, so it is recurring.

answer.text: A software update of the flight management computer system

feedback.text: No. The AD is about the landing gear pin, not avionics software.

answer.text: A one-time weight check of the forward cargo hold

feedback.text: No. It is a recurring pin inspection, and it is not one-time.

answer.text: A full replacement of both main landing gears

feedback.text: No. The action is an inspection; the improved pin comes later as the terminating action.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What does non-compliance mean for the aircraft?

generalfeedback.text: Karlis says "Non-compliance means grounding, so the aircraft may not fly until we can show compliance."

answer.text: The aircraft is grounded until they show compliance

feedback.text: Correct. It may not fly until compliance is shown.

answer.text: The airline pays a small fine but keeps flying the route

feedback.text: No. The consequence is grounding, not a fine.

answer.text: The deadline is moved to the following month

feedback.text: No. The deadline does not move; the aircraft is grounded.

answer.text: Nothing changes until the next check

feedback.text: No. Grounding follows non-compliance.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. True or false: this directive counts flight cycles, not flight hours.

generalfeedback.text: True. Karlis says "This directive counts flight cycles only, since one cycle means one takeoff and landing."

feedback.text: Correct. Cycles only — one takeoff and landing is one cycle.
Listen again: he says the directive counts cycles, not hours.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What is the recurring interval, in flight cycles? (Write the number of cycles.)

generalfeedback.text: 1500. Karlis says "The interval is fifteen hundred flight cycles, or twelve months, whichever comes first."

feedback.text: Correct — 1500 flight cycles, or 12 months, whichever comes first.
500 is the first threshold, not the recurring interval. Listen again.
12 is the number of months. The question asks for cycles: 1500.

questiontext.text: Listen to the voicemail (Dialogue 4) again. Within how many flight cycles must the first inspection be done?

generalfeedback.text: 500. The voicemail says "The first inspection must be done within five hundred flight cycles."

feedback.text: Correct — within 500 flight cycles.
1500 is the recurring interval. The first threshold is 500.
90 is the number of days in the other limit. The cycle figure is 500.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. Marta chooses the early slot. On which date does it fall?

generalfeedback.text: The second of September. Marta says "the early slot works well, because it falls on the second of September", safely before the 5 September deadline.

feedback.text: Correct — 2 September, inside the deadline.

answer.text: The fifth of September, exactly on the compliance deadline

feedback.text: No. The 5th is the deadline; the booked slot is the 2nd.
No. That is the effective date, not the slot.
No. That would be after the deadline.

questiontext.text:
Read this service-bulletin header.

SERVICE BULLETIN SB 24-1180 · ATA 24 Electrical Power · Category: RECOMMENDED · Subject: generator control unit software upgrade. Compliance: at operator discretion.

Is compliance with this document mandatory?

generalfeedback.text: No. The header marks it "RECOMMENDED" and "at operator discretion". A service bulletin is not mandatory unless an airworthiness directive makes it so.

answer.text: No — it is recommended, at operator discretion

feedback.text: Correct. Only an AD makes an action mandatory.

answer.text: Yes — every service bulletin is legally binding on the operator

feedback.text: No. A service bulletin is recommended unless an AD mandates it.

answer.text: Yes — because it lists an ATA chapter

feedback.text: No. An ATA chapter is just a subject code, not an obligation.

answer.text: No — because it has a number

feedback.text: The number is not the reason; the category "recommended" is.

questiontext.text:
Read this MEL line.

MEL 32-11: One main-gear position light may be inoperative for up to 3 days (Category C), provided the gear is confirmed down and locked by the standby indicator.

True or false: the aircraft may be dispatched with this light inoperative for a limited time, under a condition.

generalfeedback.text: True. A Minimum Equipment List (MEL) allows dispatch with certain items inoperative for a limited period, if the stated condition is met. This is different from an AD, which is a mandatory fix.

feedback.text: Correct — up to 3 days, provided the gear is confirmed down and locked.
Read again: the MEL permits limited dispatch under a condition.

questiontext.text:
Read this AD extract.

Applicability: Model A320 aircraft, serial numbers 5100 through 5140. Required action: detailed inspection of the main landing gear pivot pin within 500 flight cycles after the effective date, or 90 days, whichever comes first.

An A320 with serial number 5155 — is it affected?

generalfeedback.text: No. Applicability is 5100 through 5140. Serial 5155 is outside the range, so the AD does not apply to it. Always check the serial number against the applicability.

answer.text: No — 5155 is outside the applicability range

feedback.text: Correct. The range ends at 5140.

answer.text: Yes — every A320 in the world fleet is always affected

feedback.text: No. Only the listed serial numbers are affected.

answer.text: Yes — because it is an A320

feedback.text: Model alone is not enough; the serial must be in range.
Flight rate does not change applicability; the serial does.

questiontext.text:
Read this technical-log entry.

AD 2026-0147 first inspection of main gear pivot pin carried out. No crack found. Next inspection due at 1500 FC or 12 months. Entry quotes AD number and date. Signed: J. Ozols, Cat B1.

What does this entry prove?

generalfeedback.text: It proves compliance with the AD. A logbook or tech-log entry that quotes the AD number and date is the record an inspector uses to confirm the required action was done.

answer.text: That the AD action was done — it proves compliance

feedback.text: Correct. The entry proves compliance.

answer.text: That the aircraft is now permanently exempt from every future directive

feedback.text: No. It only records this action; recurring checks continue.

answer.text: That the AD has been cancelled

feedback.text: No. The AD is not cancelled; it was complied with.
No. This was an inspection; no crack was found.

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

Note: This AD supersedes Service Bulletin 32-0147. Do not use the superseded bulletin.

True or false: technicians should still follow the old service bulletin.

generalfeedback.text: False. "Superseded" means replaced by a newer document. The AD is now the legal order and comes first; the old bulletin must not be used.

feedback.text: No. The bulletin is superseded, so it must not be used.
Correct. Follow the AD, not the superseded bulletin.

questiontext.text:
Complete with the correct modal form (passive obligation). Write two words.

The AD is mandatory, so the inspection ______ done on time.

generalfeedback.text: must be. A passive obligation uses must + be + past participle: "must be done".

feedback.text: Correct — must be done.
Use "must be" — the pattern is must + be + past participle.

questiontext.text:
Complete so the sentence means there is no obligation (not a ban). Write two words.

After the terminating action, we ______ repeat the inspection.

generalfeedback.text: need not (or "do not have to"). Must not is a ban; need not means no obligation — you may, but nobody requires it.

feedback.text: Correct — need not repeat it.
Also correct — "do not have to" means the same.
Also correct.
That is a prohibition. Here the duty has simply ended: use "need not".
Use "need not" (or "do not have to").

questiontext.text:
Complete with a prohibition (a ban). Write two words.

You ______ fly the aircraft after the compliance deadline.

generalfeedback.text: must not. A prohibition uses must not + base verb.

feedback.text: Correct — must not fly.
Also accepted — the contracted form of must not.
Use "must not" for a ban.

questiontext.text:
Complete with the formal, written-legal modal used in directives. Write one word.

The operator ______ report compliance to the authority.

generalfeedback.text: shall. In written legal text — a directive, a work order — shall carries the binding obligation. "Must" is also acceptable in speech.

feedback.text: Correct — the register of a directive.
Accepted — "must" also states the obligation, though "shall" is the written-legal form.
Use "shall" (the written-legal form) or "must".

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the clause correctly. There is one wrong modal form.

"The AD must to be done by Friday." → The AD ______ done by Friday.

Write two words for the gap.

generalfeedback.text: must be. After must and shall never add "to": the base verb follows. Here the passive gives "must be done".

feedback.text: Correct — no "to" after must.
Drop the "to": must be done.
Write "must be" — never "must to".

name.text: U14-U6 — term: last date to comply

questiontext.text: Which two-word term means the last date to finish the required action?

generalfeedback.text: compliance deadline. It is the last date by which the AD action must be finished.

feedback.text: Correct.
Nearly — the full term is "compliance deadline".
The term is "compliance deadline".

name.text: U14-U7 — term: first action becomes due

questiontext.text: Which one-word term means the point when the very first action becomes due?

generalfeedback.text: threshold. The threshold is the first-time trigger; the interval is the gap between repeats after it.

feedback.text: Correct.
The interval is the gap between repeats. The first trigger is the "threshold".
The term is "threshold".

questiontext.text: Match each airworthiness term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: airworthiness directive = legal mandatory order · recurring inspection = a repeated check · terminating action = the final fix that ends the repeats · grounding = the aircraft may not fly · applicability = which aircraft are covered · superseded = replaced by a newer document.

answer.text: a legal order that makes a fix mandatory
a check you must repeat at set intervals
a final fix that ends the repeat requirement
the list of aircraft the directive applies to

questiontext.text: Match each term to the phrase it is used in.

generalfeedback.text: compliance deadline → meet the ...; logbook entry → sign the ...; unsafe condition → correct an ...; effective date → on the ... the clock starts; flight cycles → within 500 ...

questiontext.text: In this AD, what counts as one flight cycle?

generalfeedback.text: One takeoff and landing. That is why a daily-flying aircraft reaches the 500-cycle threshold sooner than one that flies rarely.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: One full calendar month of the aircraft being in service

feedback.text: No — that is a calendar limit, not a cycle.
No — that is a flight hour, not a cycle.
No — a cycle is a takeoff and landing.

questiontext.text: Which verb best fits: "The authority ______ an airworthiness directive"?

generalfeedback.text: issues. The authority issues (publishes) an AD; operators then show or meet compliance.

feedback.text: Correct — issue an AD.
No — the planner books a slot; the authority issues the AD.
No — a new document supersedes an old one; the authority issues the AD.
No — non-compliance grounds an aircraft; the authority issues the AD.
